approachQuestion.prompt:
Panel repaint batches. An R by C panel starts at zero. Each of m commands adds signed d to every cell in an inclusive rectangle. Return the final grid after all commands.

Input: R=2,C=3, commands [(0,0,1,1,2),(1,1,1,2,-1)]. Output: [[2,2,0],[2,1,-1]].

Constraints: 1 ≤ R,C ≤ 1000; 1 ≤ m ≤ 200000; rectangles valid with zero-based coordinates; -1000000 ≤ d ≤ 1000000. All arithmetic fits 64 bits.

Which approach handles the complete task correctly and efficiently?

options.text: Allocate a zero (R+1) by (C+1) event table. For rectangle (t,l,b,r,d) add d at (t,l) and (b+1,r+1), subtract d at (b+1,l) and (t,r+1). Accumulate across rows and then down columns, writing the first R by C entries to output.
options.feedback: The four events activate and cancel the adjustment in each dimension. Two accumulations recover precisely the covered rectangle.

options.text: Use only +d at (t,l) and -d at (b+1,r+1), then accumulate both dimensions.
options.feedback: For a 2 by 2 panel and command (0,0,0,0,1), this also changes cells (0,1) and (1,0), which must remain zero.

options.text: Visit every cell in every command rectangle and add its delta.
options.feedback: This gives correct results, but repeatedly traverses overlapping candidates. The selected summary reuses their shared work.

Four corner events make additions begin and end along both dimensions. The diagonally opposite corner restores the amount subtracted twice. Accumulating across rows and down columns expands the events into their covered rectangles.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the method in the reveal. Choose its tightest worst-case time and worst-case auxiliary-space pair. Use constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. Exclude read-only input and required output; include every described table. All loops are iterative, with no recursive stack or input copies.

options.text: O(RC + m) time; O(RC) auxiliary space
O(RC + m) time; O(1) auxiliary space
O(R + C + m) time; O(RC) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Four writes per command replace area-sized work until one final grid scan.
details: Four writes per command and two passes over the allocated table cost O(m+RC). The separate table occupies O(RC); exclude output grid.
Use constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. Exclude read-only input and required output; include every described table. All loops are iterative, with no recursive stack or input copies.

The (R+1)-by-(C+1) event table takes O(RC) initialization work for positive dimensions. Each of m commands performs four indexed updates. The two accumulation passes each visit O(RC) entries, yielding O(RC+m) total time. O(RCm) paints each command's area separately; O(R+C+m) misses the area-wide initialization and accumulation work of this fixed method.

The separate event table has (R+1)(C+1)=O(RC) 64-bit entries and is auxiliary. Loop indices and a fixed number of values add O(1). The O(1)-space option wrongly excludes the event table along with output: only the returned R-by-C grid and supplied commands are excluded, not this distinct construction table.
